author: Jerome

passages.original: Et accedentes discipuli ejus, tulerunt corpus ejus, et sepelierunt illud. Refert Josephus in quodam a Arabiae oppido Joannem capite truncatum. Et quod sequitur : Accedentes discipuli ejus, tulerunt corpus, et Ipsius Joannis, et Salvatoris discipulos possumus Intelligere.
passages.english: And his disciples came, took his body, and buried it. Josephus reports that John was beheaded in a certain town of Arabia. And as for what follows, "His disciples came and took the body," we can understand [it of] the disciples both of John himself and of the Saviour.
passages.notes: The stray "a" before "Arabiae" appears to be a footnote mark and is omitted.

passages.original: (Vers. 26.) Et videntes eum supra mare ambulan- tem, turbati sunt, dicentes : quia phantasma est. Si juxta Marcionem et Manichaeum, Dominus noster non est natus ex Virgine, sed visus in phantasmate : quomodo nunc apostoli timent ne phantasma vi- deant?
passages.english: (Verse 26.) And seeing him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying: "It is a phantom." If, according to Marcion and Manichaeus, our Lord was not born of the Virgin but was seen as a phantom, how is it that the apostles now fear that they may be seeing a phantom?

passages.original: 33.) Qui autem in navicula erant, venerunt et adoraverunt eum, dicentes : Vere Filius Dei es. Ad unum signum tranquillitate maris reddita, quae post nimias procellas interdum et casu fieri solet, nautae atque vectores vere Filium Dei confitentur, et Arius in Ecclesia praedicat creaturam.
passages.english: 33.) But those who were in the boat came and worshipped him, saying: "Truly you are the Son of God." At a single sign, the calming of the sea, which after excessive storms sometimes happens even by chance, the sailors and passengers confess [him] truly the Son of God, and Arius in the Church preaches [him] a creature.
passages.notes: The verse heading is split from the preceding context; it reads "(Verse 33.)".

passages.original: (Vers. 51.) Et ecce velum Templi scissum est in duas partes a summo usque deorsum. Velum templi scissum est, et omnia Legis sacramenta quae prius tegebantur, prodita sunt, atque ad Gentium popu- lum transierunt. In Evangelio, cujus saepe facimus mentionem, superliminare templi infinitae magnitu- dinis fractum 237 esse atque divisum legimus [Al. legi]. Josephus quoque refert virtutes Angelicas, praesides quondam templi, (??) tunc pariter concla- masse : Transeamus ex his sedibus.
passages.english: (Verse 51.) And behold, the veil of the Temple was torn in two, from top to bottom. The veil of the temple was torn, and all the sacraments of the Law which had previously been covered were laid open and passed over to the people of the Gentiles. In the Gospel which we often mention, we read [variant: I have read] that the lintel of the temple, of immense size, was broken and split. Josephus also reports that the angelic powers, once the guardians of the temple, then cried out together: "Let us depart from these seats."
passages.notes: "237" is a page number from the printed edition and is omitted. "(??)" marks an uncertain point in the edition's text; the sentence reads coherently without it. "[Al. legi]" records a variant reading ("I have read" for "we read"). "The Gospel which we often mention" is presumably the Gospel according to the Hebrews, which Jerome cites elsewhere; it is not named here.
